run1.note: mixes device (Fez -> Kingston) and design (no resets, XY4, twirl, 5.8-6.0 us rounds against 7.9 us); the model's design effect alone, on Kingston, is predicted_prerun.design_effect_model_as_sent_over_run1_design

caveats: IBM's 20:27 calibration, which the pre-run prediction, the decoders and the model at the measured T_q all use, has data 72 at 20.2% and data 12 at 18.5% readout error; 21:55's has 5.1% and 4.4%, and the idle test's offsets r/G (1.53 and 1.45) put them near 5% during the jobs. The model therefore overstates those two qubits' readout; readout_sensitivity holds the model with 21:55's readout and with 21:55's whole calibration.
IBM's 21:55 calibration differs from 20:27's in readout only (155 qubits), so model_ro and model_after are the same model.

The jobs differ: d=3 X eps 7.2 vs 5.9% (2.4 sigma), driven by flag 93 reading 1 about 13 points more often in exp1-1 (its X4X7 / X16X21 detectors 20% vs 8%; data 92 beside it had idle contrast 0.66 of the model's in exp1-1, 1.10 in exp1-2), and in exp1-2 relays 15 and 35 (d=5 only) reading 1 14-20 points more often (relay Z24Z25 detector 4.7% to 11.1%). Both jobs pooled is the plan's estimate.

T_q is the XY4-decoupled, twirled decay on the model's clock, not IBM's Hahn T2; 11 of 25 rates move by more than 3 sigma between the jobs 35 min apart, so the pooled T_q carries a systematic spread beyond its sigma.

Flag and relay records here are F_t = f_t XOR the previous readout (no resets); run 1's were raw readouts after reset, and its circuits had 8 rounds of 7.9 us (here 4 rounds of 5.8-6.0 us), so the 4-round HMM's exit rate is weakly determined and often sits on its 0.5 cap in the model.
eps_new/eps_run1 mixes device (Fez to Kingston) and design (no resets, XY4, twirl, shorter rounds); per round, not per us.
Binomial dispersion above 1 (Z d=5 1.38 at cap 0.1; correlated Z 2.6/2.0; uniform Z d=3 1.9) widens those intervals: the 4-point curves are not exactly (1-2 eps)^n.
